The Telegraph (Martin Evans, Crime Editor; Rozina Sabur, National Security Editor; Tim Sigsworth) — published 29 September 2026 1:47pm BST, confirmed from the in-article line "Published 29 September 2026 1:47pm BST". Search highlights.
"RAF plot 'may have been a dry run'"
Five men arrested on suspicion of a bomb plot near RAF Fairford may have been conducting a "dry run". British nationals, all in their 20s, detained near the base on Sunday on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offences; released on bail after being questioned for less than 36 hours. On Tuesday, a FORMER counter-terrorism officer (unnamed in the highlight) said detectives would be assessing whether the suspects had been engaged in a dry run — this is expert speculation, NOT a police claim.
The three vans were found 400m from the Gloucestershire air base and were examined by Army bomb disposal specialists and a robot.
ASST COMMISSIONER LAURENCE TAYLOR: the suspects were bailed "following extensive interviews and inquiries"; "They absolutely remain under investigation as we explore multiple lines of inquiry." Outside Scotland Yard on Monday he said officers were "keeping an open mind" but one line of inquiry was that "this may be activity committed by proxies, or individuals either knowingly or unknowingly, working on behalf of a foreign state".
RAF Fairford is a joint US military base which American forces have used to conduct defensive strikes on Iran in recent months.
